belief: If I just prayed more, I wouldn't feel this way.
origins: Well-meaning people may say, “Just pray about it,” or “Give it to God,” leaving the suffering person feeling guilty. They pray more, feel no relief, and conclude that something is wrong with them or with their faith.
teaches: Elijah, discouraged, prayed that he might die, and God did not rebuke him. He sent an angel who said, “Get up and eat,” and let him sleep. Paul prayed three times about his thorn, and God answered, “My grace is sufficient for you.” David prayed often and still wrote, “Why are you downcast, O my soul?” Prayer is vital, and it often brings peace. But God also gives rest, food, friends, doctors, and counselors. Continued pain is not proof of insufficient prayer.
self_statements: If I had more faith, I would feel better.
My prayers must not be good enough.
Something is wrong with my relationship with God.
I should not feel this way.
errors: Believing prayer either removes feelings completely or has failed.
Feeling unrelieved and concluding that I prayed wrongly.
questions: Who told me that prayer should remove these feelings?
How did God care for Elijah when he was despairing?
What other help might God have provided for me?
What do I need besides prayer, such as rest, food, friends, or counsel?
What did David do with feelings that persisted?
What is one practical step I can add to prayer?
truth: Prayer matters, and so do rest, food, friends, and professional help. Persisting feelings do not prove failed faith. I can pray honestly and also care for myself and seek help.
hw_truths: God cared for Elijah with rest and food.
His grace is sufficient for me.
David prayed and still felt downcast.
Prayer and practical help work together.
Feelings that persist are not proof of failed faith.
log: Each week, note one prayer and one practical step of care.
actions: Tell God exactly how you feel.
Notice how God cared for Elijah.
hw_questions: How did God care for Elijah?
What other help might He give?
What do I need besides prayer?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God cared for Elijah with rest and food, and He cares for me.”

prayer: Lord, I am weary and still struggling. Thank You for caring for me as You did Elijah. Help me pray honestly and receive the help You provide. Amen.
